svg.title: Forest Cover Lab: problems and approaches
svg.desc: 8 problems in forest-cover estimation (Annual labels are not monthly truth; “Forest” is ambiguous; Area depends on projection; Monthly signal is noisy; Model value is unknown locally; Platform lock-in; Agent plans are not observed execution; Knowledge and repos drift) mapped to the repository approaches that address them, plus the v1, v2, v3 roadmap.
svg.text: Forest Cover Lab — problems and how the repo addresses them
Governance, research and evidence registry for forest-cover estimation from satellite data. Executable workflows live in downstream repos.
⚠ Binding constraint: Hansen annual loss ≠ monthly ground truth. Monthly forest cover is never reported as verified when derived from annual weak labels.
Annual labels are not monthly truth
Hansen lossyear says a pixel was lost in a year, not in
which month. Training and scoring monthly models on
it leaks labels and overclaims accuracy.
Monthly coverage, monthly disturbance probability and annual supervision are distinct
concepts. v3 treats monthly state as latent, pools monthly events to the annual bag (e.g.
noisy-OR) and reports agreement as consistency, not accuracy.
Area numbers are meaningless when the threshold,
minimum mapping area, exclusions and nodata
handling are left implicit or hardcoded.
Every run declares dataset, threshold variable and value, minimum mapping area,
exclusions, nodata policy and temporal interpretation; defaults live in config, never in code.
Pixel counts in EPSG:4326 or a conformal CRS distort
hectares, especially away from the equator.
Exchange geometries in EPSG:4326; compute area in an equal-area CRS (EPSG:6933
globally) or geodesically; always report hectares and the method used.
Clouds, seasonal browning and single-month anomalies
trigger false alerts; optical and SAR evidence can
Cloud-masked monthly S2 and S1 composites; NDVI/NDMI anomalies confirmed by SAR
backscatter; an N-consecutive-month persistence rule; per-pixel optical/SAR disagreement
Eight GeoFM families look promising, but none is
integrated or benchmarked; published scores do not
transfer to a local forest-loss task.
Compare B0 (current rules), B1 (raw-feature model) and F1–F4 (frozen encoder, adaptation,
fusion, stacking) on independent, spatially and temporally blocked reference samples with
Production methods tied to Google Earth Engine cannot
be reproduced or run independently at regional or
Open, local, cloud-neutral tooling for production (STAC, GDAL/rasterio, xarray, DuckDB); GEE
remains an optional reference or research route.
A selected role or host name does not prove which
instructions were loaded, which tools ran or whether
Proposed standing role contracts plus bounded assignments; an explicit agent graph shows
what each agent passes on and where humans approve; record actual hosts, pinned
repositories, loaded-file hashes, evidence and checks. Human review governs scientific
Evidence gets scattered, downstream repos redefine
contracts, and agents can turn a proposal or a
Knowledge corpus + deterministic graph; agent output enters as candidate and needs
human review to promote; run manifests with semantic provenance; drift checklist and audit
GeoFM uplift, local accuracy and model rankings are currently not measured; candidate methods stay candidates until human review promotes them.
